pki.refuse.key_in_chain: The chain file holds a private key; upload the key as a separate file
pki.refuse.chain_unreadable: Certificate {n} of the chain cannot be read: {err}
pki.refuse.no_chain: No PEM certificate in the chain file (it should start with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----)
pki.refuse.chain_too_long: A chain may have at most {max} certificates
pki.refuse.key_mismatch: The private key does not match the first certificate of the chain (the server certificate): the chain must start with the server certificate, and the key must be its key
pki.refuse.self_signed_inside: Certificate {n} is self-signed; it may only be the last of the chain
pki.refuse.order: Certificate {n} is not issued by certificate {next}: the chain must be in the order server certificate, intermediate certificates, root certificate ({err})
pki.refuse.no_key: No PEM private key in the key file (it should start with -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- or similar)
pki.refuse.key_encrypted: The private key is encrypted. Upload an unencrypted key (for example after openssl pkey -in key.pem -out key-plain.pem)
pki.refuse.key_unreadable: The private key cannot be read: {err}
pki.refuse.key_type: Only RSA and ECDSA keys are supported
pki.refuse.no_server_auth: The server certificate may not be used for server authentication: its extended key usage (EKU) lacks serverAuth
pki.refuse.no_san: The server certificate has no subject alternative names (SAN); phones check only the names in the SAN
pki.refuse.no_public_host: The certificate does not name the public host {host} (names in the certificate: {names})
pki.unused.https_files: uses the certificate files named in the environment
pki.unused.https_proxy: is provided by the reverse proxy
pki.unused.ldap_files: LDAP uses the certificate files named in the environment
pki.refuse.unused: No service would use this certificate: HTTPS {https}, {ldap} (names in the certificate: {names})
pki.refuse.no_anchor: The chain is not trusted by a public CA and holds no root certificate, so phones cannot trust it. Add the root certificate that issued it (the self-signed CA certificate) at the end of the chain and upload again
pki.warn.no_ldap_host: The certificate does not name the LDAP address {host}: LDAP keeps the certificate of the built-in CA, which goes on issuing.
pki.warn.empty_aki: Chain certificates with an empty AuthorityKeyIdentifier extension: {n}. The phones’ SIP/LDAP TLS library (mbedTLS 3.6.0) aborts the handshake, so LDAP directories and SIP TLS connections that use these certificates will fail. Use certificates without this empty extension.
pki.warn.self_signed_leaf: This is a self-signed server certificate (not a CA). Phones trust it directly when they scan, so every phone must scan again when it is replaced.
pki.warn.rescan_import: Bound devices that trust the issuer of the current HTTPS certificate: {n}. The new certificate is neither issued by it nor trusted by a public CA. Once it is in use these devices cannot sync until their QR codes are regenerated and scanned again.
pki.warn.reprint: The pin in QR codes will change. Pending clients whose printed or sent QR codes stop working: {n}. Print or send them again (QR codes on the platform’s pages update themselves).
pki.warn.rescan_remove: Bound devices that trust the issuer of the own certificate, not the built-in CA: {n}. Once it is removed these devices cannot sync until their QR codes are regenerated and scanned again.
pki.notice.expired: The certificate has expired; phones cannot sync ({cert} expired on {date})
pki.notice.expires: {cert} expires on {date} (days left: {days}); replace it in time
pki.paused: Issuing is paused: no service uses a certificate of the built-in CA
pki.mode.none: No TLS (HTTPS from the reverse proxy, LDAP off)
pki.mode.own_and_files: Own certificate and certificate files from the environment (issuing paused)
pki.mode.mixed: Mixed: some services use certificates of the built-in CA (issuing goes on)
pki.mode.files: Certificate files from the environment (issuing paused)
